title: The compact-support bound uses the original fibres
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type
schemes over a field, with geometric fibres of dimension at most $d$.
Let $A$ be a finite ring whose additive exponent is invertible on
$Y$. For every etale $A$-module sheaf $F$, its
compact-support direct image
satisfies

$$
R^qf_!F=0\qquad(q>2d).
$$

All functors here act on ordinary
derived categories.

proof.text: The existing source declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isZero_homology_rightDerivedLowerShriek_singleFunctor_of_two_mul_lt in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.Finiteness.CohomologicalDimension already realizes this blueprint lemma for dimension bounds at all separably closed field-valued points. Reuse that declaration rather than restating its substantial proof. Its mathematical argument remains the following nine steps. To supply its stronger-looking fibre hypothesis from the present canonical-algebraic-closure hypothesis, factor each field-valued point Spec Omega -> Y through Spec kappa(y), using Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField. Pullback associativity identifies its fibre with the base change of f.fiber y. Dimension preservation under field extension, topologicalKrullDim_pullback_eq_of_field (the closed source realization of lem-pc-dim-base-change), identifies both this dimension and the canonical algebraic-closure fibre dimension with dim(f.fiber y). Transport the given bound through these two equalities. This also handles empty fibres without a nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: topologicalKrullDim_pullback_eq_of_field; field-valued fibre factorization as in topologicalKrullDim_pullback_le

proof.text: A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Hence $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. In particular $Y$ is quasi-compact, and it is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to the given separated finite-type $f$ to choose a factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ with $j$ open and $r$ proper. Proper includes finite type, so the same Noetherian lemma shows that $\overline X$ is Noetherian. By [def-amb-etale-compact-support] the chosen candidate on $F[0]$ is $Rr_*j_!F$, and [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] identifies this candidate with $Rf_!F$. This application uses only bounded-below objects: $j_!F$ is a sheaf in degree zero. The ordinary unbounded and bounded-below computations agree here: [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] gives a bounded-below injective resolution of this sheaf which is K-injective, and both [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] compute $Rr_*$ by applying $r_*$ to that same resolution.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: choose a compactification and compute the ordinary compact-support candidate

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$, choose the geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ with $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(y)}$, and put $T=\overline X_{\bar y}$ and $U=X_{\bar y}$. The base-changed map $j_{\bar y}:U\to T$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Write $F_{\bar y}$ for the inverse image of $F$ on $U$. The first, derived-category clause of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite], applied to $r$ and $j_!F[0]$, and [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] give $\bar y^{-1}Rf_!F\simeq Ra_{T,*}G$, where $G=j_{\bar y!}F_{\bar y}$ and $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Here the corollary allows every $K\in D^+(\overline X_{\Et},A)$; its later clause for finite module sheaves is not being applied to the possibly infinite sheaf $F$. Inverse image of constant-ring module sheaves is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], hence commutes with cohomology of complexes (preserve kernels, images and cokernels). On $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, sections at the identity etale object equal the geometric stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant-stalk], compatibly with addition and scalar multiplication because the map is restriction of sections. Thus sections there are exact, and taking degree $q$ of the displayed derived isomorphism gives $(R^qf_!F)_{\bar y}\cong H^q_A(T,G)$: on an injective resolution of $G$, sections of $a_{T,*}$ are precisely sections on $T$, by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] identifies the underlying abelian group of this module cohomology with $H^q(T,G_{ab})$, where $G_{ab}$ is the underlying abelian sheaf.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: geometric-stalk formula, including extension-by-zero base change and coefficient forgetting

proof.text: By [lem-pc-proper-base-change], $T\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is proper. Therefore $T$ is finite type over $\Omega$ by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Let $|C|$ be the closure of the open subset $|U|$ in $|T|$, and equip it with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $i:C\hookrightarrow T$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $C$ is proper over $\Omega$, hence finite type. The closed subset $|C|$ has finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]. Equip each component with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure in $T$ using the same construction; each is again proper and finite type over $\Omega$. It is integral by the reduced-and-irreducible characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. These assertions concern the closed subscheme structures in $T$; no factorization of the possibly nonreduced scheme $U$ through the reduced scheme $C$ is asserted.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph, first sentence: reduced closure of the original fibre and its finite-type components

proof.text: Every $C_a$ meets $|U|$. If $C_a\cap |U|$ were empty, then $|U|$ would be contained in the finite union of the other irreducible components. That union is closed, so it would also contain the closure $|C|$ of $|U|$, contradicting that $C_a$ is an irreducible component and is not contained in the union of the other components. Thus $V_a=C_a\cap |U|$ is nonempty. It is open in the integral finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $C_a$, so [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] gives $\dim C_a=\dim V_a$. Also $V_a$ is closed in $|U|$, because $C_a$ is closed in $|T|$. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of $V_a$ is therefore such a chain in $|U|$. By [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the fibre hypothesis, $\dim C_a=\dim V_a\leq\dim U\leq d$. This uses the integral finite-type dimension theorem, rather than asserting that an arbitrary dense open in an arbitrary Noetherian scheme has the same dimension.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: dimension of a component equals the dimension of its nonempty open in the original fibre (Stacks Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, part (3))

proof.text: If $C$ is nonempty, any finite strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $|C|$ lies in one of the components $C_a$: its largest member is irreducible and the finite family of closed subsets $C_a$ covers $|C|$, so that largest member lies in one $C_a$. All members of the chain are closed and irreducible in $C_a$ as well, and all its strict inclusions are unchanged. The component bound from the previous step and [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] show $\dim C\leq d$. If $C$ is empty, then $U$ is empty and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] makes $G_{ab}$ zero at every geometric point of $T$; [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to $0\to G_{ab}$ gives $G_{ab}=0$, hence all its cohomology groups are zero by the zero resolution in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. In this case the stalk in step 2 already vanishes. Henceforth suppose $C$ nonempty.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: pass from component bounds to the closed-support bound; explicit empty-fibre case

proof.text: The stalk formula of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] says that $G_{ab}$ is zero outside $|U|$, hence outside $|C|$. Apply [lem-kun-04ca] to the actual closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow T$: there is an abelian sheaf $H$ on $C_{\Et}$ with $G_{ab}\cong i_*H$, and its left-inverse clause permits $H\cong i^{-1}G_{ab}$. Let $N\geq1$ be the additive exponent of the finite coefficient ring $A$. Then $N$ kills every $A$-module, since $(N\cdot1_A)m=0$, so it kills $G_{ab}$. The additive exact inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] shows that $N$ kills $H$ as well. In particular $H$ is a torsion abelian sheaf, without any finiteness or constructibility assumption on its stalks.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: extension by zero is a closed direct image from its reduced closed support (Stacks Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward)

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] to the abelian sheaf $H$: for every $q\geq0$ it gives $H^q(T,G_{ab})\cong H^q(T,i_*H)\cong H^q(C,H)$. This cites the cohomology comparison itself, not merely exactness of closed direct image.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: compute cohomology on the closed support (Stacks Tag 035C, lemma-closed-immersion-finite; Tag 0A5D, lemma-finite-pushforward-statements)

proof.text: The field $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed: a nonconstant separable polynomial has a root in $\Omega$. Therefore [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] supplies $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\Omega)\leq0$ in exactly the sense of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]. Apply [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] to the nonempty finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $C$ with $e=\dim C\leq d$. It gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(C)\leq2e$. Since $H$ is torsion, the definition yields $H^q(C,H)=0$ whenever $q>2d\geq2e$. By steps 2 and 7 the stalk $(R^qf_!F)_{\bar y}$ is zero. Invertibility of the exponent is among the hypotheses stated in the item and is retained; this particular torsion cohomological-dimension argument does not require a stronger coefficient hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: vanishing above twice the dimension of the closed support, with the precise torsion cohomological-dimension convention

proof.text: For fixed $q>2d$, the preceding argument applies to the chosen algebraic closure over every point $y$ of $Y$. By [lem-kun-support-geometric-point-independent], vanishing at that geometric stalk implies vanishing at every geometric point over $y$. Thus all geometric stalks of the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qf_!F$ vanish. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the morphism from the zero sheaf to this underlying sheaf: it is an isomorphism. An $A$-module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is the zero module sheaf, since its groups of sections and all its structure maps are zero. Therefore $R^qf_!F=0$. Only $\dim U$ and the dimension of its closed support were bounded; no bound was imposed on the entire compactified fibre $T$.

source.place: Proof, last sentences: geometric stalks detect zero; no bound on the entire compactified fibre

proof.text: Apply the existing source amplitude declaration with the actual structure morphisms X -> Spec k and Y -> Spec k; comp_over supplies their compatibility with f. Supply the locally Noetherian and compact-space instances for Y, hence Nagata compactifiability. Its output is for HasCompactification.compactification f. Place F in DerivedCategory.Plus with singleFunctor at degree zero. The bounded-below compactification comparison rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusιIso identifies the candidate from compactSupportAmplitudeCompactification with this chosen candidate on that input. Apply homologyFunctor.mapIso and IsZero.of_iso to obtain exactly the displayed unbounded-derived-category conclusion. No unbounded compactification-independence assertion is needed.
